title: P30-family attention sink: a learned per-head sink key with a zero value in all six Peri-LN blocks, on the 115-fable hybrid ALiBi/NoPE Lean incumbent (4,801,536 params)
description: P30 family (suppressible retrieval): every attention head gets one learned, zero-initialised sink key with a zero value, prepended to its keys, so a head can put its softmax mass on 'nothing' instead of spreading it over irrelevant keys. Expert iteration samples proofs of 7+ lines, longer than any pretraining sequence, where the four NoPE content-lookup heads (115) have more distractor keys and no way to abstain; an abstain option should keep their residual writes clean at those lengths and give RL a better-formed start.
hypothesis: Softmax forces every head to write a convex mix of values. For 115's NoPE heads (content lookup of a name's binding at any distance) a query with no matching key, or a sequence longer than pretraining saw, spreads mass over many irrelevant keys and adds noise to the residual stream, which the downstream Peri-LN renormalises rather than suppresses. A learned input-dependent sink lets each head abstain per query, so attention outputs stay length-robust. Prediction: round-1 RL targets solved at or above 115's 718/756/691 with round-1 parse failures at or below 115's 25/22/18%, eval ge10/ge11 counts not lower, and a metric near or above 631.33. Pretraining cost: three cats per block, expected 1-5% fewer steps (115: 4204 on seed 0); val loss about 115's (0.080-0.086). If the round-1 start does not improve, the mechanism is not supported even if the mean moves.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads (115-fable), plus CHANGED: a learned per-head attention-sink key with a zero value in every block
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (CHANGED from 113's all-ALiBi): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: only the sink key parameter in PeriLNBlock.__init__ and three torch.cat lines in PeriLNBlock.attn (k, v, mask). Slopes, ALiBiGPT, width, heads, depth, GELU, init of every other parameter, optimizer, schedule, batch and data are byte-identical to 115
arch.n_params_detail: 4,800,000 (115-fable) + 6 blocks x 8 heads x 32 = 1,536 sink-key parameters = 4,801,536 (vocab 107)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py, replace blocks with this file's PeriLNBlock (which owns sink_k), then load state (115's keys plus blocks.i.sink_k). The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: unchanged cache contents (sink never stored). CPU check with the pinned fork 51604b3 and sink keys set to N(0, 0.5): 2-sequence prefill of 20 tokens plus 20 cached one-token steps vs the full forward, max abs logit diff 8.3e-7; backward runs and sink_k receives gradient; 4,801,536 params; sink_k is not in the Muon matrix list
arch.attention_sink: CHANGED: each PeriLNBlock has sink_k, a Parameter of shape (1, 8, 1, 32) (one key per head), zero-initialised. Every attention call prepends it to the keys (after the KV cache is read, so it is never cached), prepends a zero vector to the values and a 0 column to the additive ALiBi/causal mask. The sink logit is q_h . sink_h / sqrt(32) with no positional term, so each head can send attention mass to a slot that contributes nothing (softmax off by one at init, input-dependent once learned; cf. gpt-oss 2025 learned sinks, Xiao et al. 2023 StreamingLLM, Miller 2023 softmax1). Persists into RL and eval (it is part of the model).

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
optimizer.sink_parameters: CHANGED: the 6 sink_k tensors are 4-D, so they fall in the AdamW auxiliary group (lr 1e-3 schedule, wd 0.1, betas 0.9/0.95), not Muon, and are not touched by the orthogonal init loop (2-D only)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1; CHANGED: sink_k zeros (sink logit 0 for every query at init)
